title.en: Prove undecidability by reduction from the halting problem
title.zh: 通过从停机问题归约来证明不可判定

prompt.en:
Notation: ⟨M⟩ is a string encoding the Turing machine M, and ⟨M,w⟩ encodes M together with an input w. HALT = { ⟨M,w⟩ : M halts on input w }. You may use that HALT is undecidable. A decider is a Turing machine that halts on every input; a machine "accepts 01" if it halts in its accept state on the input 01.

Let ACC01 = { ⟨M⟩ : M accepts the string 01 }. Prove that ACC01 is undecidable by reduction from HALT: assume a decider D for ACC01 exists and use it to build a decider for HALT. Describe the machine you build from ⟨M,w⟩, explain why building it is a mechanical (computable) step, and prove that the construction is correct in both cases (M halts on w, M does not halt on w).
prompt.zh:
记号：⟨M⟩ 是图灵机 M 的编码串，⟨M,w⟩ 是 M 与输入 w 一起的编码。HALT = { ⟨M,w⟩ : M 在输入 w 上停机 }。可以使用 HALT 不可判定这一事实。判定器是对每个输入都停机的图灵机；若机器在输入 01 上停机于接受状态，就说它“接受 01”。

令 ACC01 = { ⟨M⟩ : M 接受字符串 01 }。通过从 HALT 归约来证明 ACC01 不可判定：假设存在 ACC01 的判定器 D，并用它造出 HALT 的判定器。描述你由 ⟨M,w⟩ 构造的机器，解释这一构造是机械的（可计算的），并在两种情形（M 在 w 上停机、M 在 w 上不停机）下证明构造正确。

solution.en:
Assume, for contradiction, that D is a decider for ACC01. We build a machine H that decides HALT.

Construction. Given ⟨M,w⟩, H first writes down the description of a new machine M_w:
M_w on input x: ignore x; simulate M on the fixed input w; if the simulation halts (in any way), accept.
The description of M_w is built from ⟨M⟩ and w by copying M's rules, adding a few start-up rules that write w on the tape, and changing M's halting states so that they lead to the accept state of M_w. This is a purely mechanical transformation of text, so H can do it, and it always finishes.

Then H runs D on ⟨M_w⟩. If D accepts, H accepts; if D rejects, H rejects.

Correctness.
Case 1: M halts on w. Then M_w, on every input x, finishes the simulation and accepts. In particular it accepts 01, so ⟨M_w⟩ ∈ ACC01 and D accepts. H accepts, which is right because ⟨M,w⟩ ∈ HALT.
Case 2: M does not halt on w. Then M_w runs forever on every input x, so it never accepts 01. Thus ⟨M_w⟩ ∉ ACC01 and D rejects. H rejects, which is right because ⟨M,w⟩ ∉ HALT.

H halts on every input: the construction of ⟨M_w⟩ finishes, and D halts because it is a decider. (Strings that are not valid encodings are rejected at the start.) So H is a decider for HALT. But HALT is undecidable, a contradiction. Hence no decider D for ACC01 exists, and ACC01 is undecidable. ∎

Note that M_w does not look at its input: it behaves the same on every x, so asking whether it accepts the one string 01 is as hard as asking whether M halts on w. (ACC01 is still recognizable: simulate M on 01 and accept if M accepts.)
solution.zh:
假设（用于反证）D 是 ACC01 的判定器。我们来造一台判定 HALT 的机器 H。

构造。给定 ⟨M,w⟩，H 首先写出一台新机器 M_w 的描述：
M_w 在输入 x 上：忽略 x；在固定输入 w 上模拟 M；如果模拟停机（无论以何种方式），就接受。
M_w 的描述由 ⟨M⟩ 和 w 得到：复制 M 的规则，加上若干启动规则把 w 写到纸带上，并把 M 的停机状态改成通向 M_w 的接受状态。这只是对文本的机械变换，所以 H 能做到，而且它一定会结束。

然后 H 在 ⟨M_w⟩ 上运行 D。若 D 接受，H 就接受；若 D 拒绝，H 就拒绝。

正确性。
情形 1：M 在 w 上停机。那么 M_w 对每个输入 x 都会完成模拟并接受。特别地，它接受 01，所以 ⟨M_w⟩ ∈ ACC01，D 接受。H 接受，这是对的，因为 ⟨M,w⟩ ∈ HALT。
情形 2：M 在 w 上不停机。那么 M_w 对每个输入 x 都永远运行，所以它从不接受 01。因此 ⟨M_w⟩ ∉ ACC01，D 拒绝。H 拒绝，这是对的，因为 ⟨M,w⟩ ∉ HALT。

H 对每个输入都停机：⟨M_w⟩ 的构造会结束，D 是判定器所以会停机。（不是合法编码的字符串一开始就被拒绝。）所以 H 是 HALT 的判定器。但 HALT 不可判定，矛盾。因此不存在 ACC01 的判定器 D，ACC01 不可判定。∎

注意，M_w 不看它的输入：对所有 x 行为相同，所以问它是否接受 01 这一个字符串，与问 M 是否在 w 上停机一样难。（ACC01 仍然是可识别的：在 01 上模拟 M，若 M 接受就接受。）

text.en: Setup: assumes a decider D for ACC01 and states the plan to decide HALT; uses that HALT is undecidable.
text.zh: 起步：假设 ACC01 有判定器 D，并说明用它判定 HALT 的计划；使用 HALT 不可判定的事实。

text.en: Construction of M_w from ⟨M,w⟩: ignores its input, simulates M on w, accepts if it halts; explains this construction is computable.
text.zh: 由 ⟨M,w⟩ 构造 M_w：忽略输入，在 w 上模拟 M，停机就接受；并说明这一构造是可计算的。

text.en: Correctness in both cases: M halts ⇒ M_w accepts everything including 01; M does not halt ⇒ M_w accepts nothing.
text.zh: 两种情形的正确性：M 停机 ⇒ M_w 接受一切（包括 01）；M 不停机 ⇒ M_w 什么都不接受。

text.en: H always halts and decides HALT; contradiction; concludes ACC01 is undecidable.
text.zh: H 总是停机并判定 HALT；产生矛盾；得出 ACC01 不可判定。

mistakes.en: Building M_w that simulates M on its own input x instead of on w: then M_w's behaviour on 01 only tells us about M on 01, not about ⟨M,w⟩.
mistakes.zh: 构造的 M_w 在自己的输入 x 上模拟 M，而不是在 w 上模拟：这样 M_w 在 01 上的行为只反映 M 在 01 上的情形，与 ⟨M,w⟩ 无关。

mistakes.en: Running M on w inside H (instead of building M_w): if M loops, H loops and is not a decider.
mistakes.zh: 在 H 里直接运行 M 于 w（而不是构造 M_w）：若 M 循环，H 也循环，就不是判定器。

mistakes.en: Reducing in the wrong direction (from ACC01 to HALT), which proves nothing about ACC01.
mistakes.zh: 归约方向弄反（从 ACC01 归约到 HALT），这对 ACC01 什么也证明不了。

mistakes.en: Not explaining that the construction of M_w is computable.
mistakes.zh: 没有说明 M_w 的构造是可计算的。

questions.verify_output:
rejects after 7 steps: M halts = True ; M_w accepts 01 = True ; M_w treats every input alike = True
accepts after 3 steps: M halts = True ; M_w accepts 01 = True ; M_w treats every input alike = True
loops forever: M halts = False ; M_w accepts 01 = False ; M_w treats every input alike = True

title.en: Undecidability of deciding whether two machines are equivalent
title.zh: 两台机器是否等价的问题不可判定

prompt.en:
Notation: L(M) is the set of strings that the Turing machine M accepts. ⟨M1,M2⟩ encodes a pair of machines. EQ = { ⟨M1,M2⟩ : L(M1) = L(M2) }. HALT = { ⟨M,w⟩ : M halts on w } is undecidable, and you may use this. A decider is a Turing machine that halts on every input.

Prove that EQ is undecidable by reduction from HALT. Assume a decider E for EQ. Build, from ⟨M,w⟩, two machines M1 and M2 such that L(M1) = L(M2) exactly when M halts on w, and use E to decide HALT. Prove that the construction is correct in both cases.
prompt.zh:
记号：L(M) 是图灵机 M 所接受的字符串的集合。⟨M1,M2⟩ 是一对机器的编码。EQ = { ⟨M1,M2⟩ : L(M1) = L(M2) }。HALT = { ⟨M,w⟩ : M 在 w 上停机 } 不可判定，可以使用这一事实。判定器是对每个输入都停机的图灵机。

通过从 HALT 归约证明 EQ 不可判定。假设 EQ 有判定器 E。由 ⟨M,w⟩ 构造两台机器 M1 和 M2，使得当且仅当 M 在 w 上停机时 L(M1) = L(M2)，并用 E 判定 HALT。在两种情形下证明构造正确。

solution.en:
Assume, for contradiction, that E is a decider for EQ. We build a decider H for HALT.

Construction. Given ⟨M,w⟩, H writes the descriptions of two machines:
M1 on input x: ignore x; simulate M on w; if the simulation halts, accept.
M2 on input x: accept immediately.
Both descriptions are produced mechanically from ⟨M,w⟩ (M2 is the same for every input to H; M1 copies M with a few extra rules, as in the usual reduction), so this step always finishes. Then H runs E on ⟨M1,M2⟩ and gives E's answer.

Correctness.
Case 1: M halts on w. Then M1 accepts every x, and so does M2, so L(M1) = L(M2) = Σ*. E accepts, so H accepts. Correct.
Case 2: M does not halt on w. Then M1 never accepts anything (it loops forever on every x), so L(M1) = ∅, while L(M2) = Σ*. These differ (Σ* has at least one string, namely ε). E rejects, so H rejects. Correct.

H always halts, because the construction finishes and E is a decider. So H decides HALT, which contradicts the undecidability of HALT. Hence there is no decider for EQ, and EQ is undecidable. ∎

Remark. Fixing M2 as the machine that accepts everything turns "are the two languages equal?" into "does M1 accept everything?", and M1 accepts everything exactly when the simulation of M on w ends. The same trick shows that deciding L(M) = Σ* is undecidable.
solution.zh:
假设（用于反证）E 是 EQ 的判定器。我们造 HALT 的判定器 H。

构造。给定 ⟨M,w⟩，H 写出两台机器的描述：
M1 在输入 x 上：忽略 x；在 w 上模拟 M；若模拟停机，就接受。
M2 在输入 x 上：立即接受。
两个描述都由 ⟨M,w⟩ 机械地产生（M2 对 H 的每个输入都相同；M1 复制 M 并加上几条规则，与通常的归约一样），所以这一步一定会结束。然后 H 在 ⟨M1,M2⟩ 上运行 E，并给出 E 的答案。

正确性。
情形 1：M 在 w 上停机。那么 M1 接受每个 x，M2 也是，所以 L(M1) = L(M2) = Σ*。E 接受，所以 H 接受。正确。
情形 2：M 在 w 上不停机。那么 M1 什么也不接受（它对每个 x 都永远循环），所以 L(M1) = ∅，而 L(M2) = Σ*。二者不同（Σ* 至少含一个字符串，例如 ε）。E 拒绝，所以 H 拒绝。正确。

H 总是停机，因为构造会结束而 E 是判定器。所以 H 判定 HALT，这与 HALT 不可判定矛盾。因此 EQ 没有判定器，EQ 不可判定。∎

注：把 M2 固定为“接受一切”的机器，就把“两个语言是否相等”变成“M1 是否接受一切”，而 M1 接受一切当且仅当对 M 在 w 上的模拟结束。同样的技巧说明，判定 L(M) = Σ* 也是不可判定的。

text.en: Setup: assumes a decider E for EQ and plans to decide HALT with it.
text.zh: 起步：假设 EQ 有判定器 E，并计划用它判定 HALT。

text.en: Constructs M1 (ignores input, simulates M on w, accepts if it halts) and M2 (accepts everything); notes that both are computable from ⟨M,w⟩.
text.zh: 构造 M1（忽略输入，在 w 上模拟 M，停机就接受）和 M2（接受一切）；并指出二者都可由 ⟨M,w⟩ 计算出来。

text.en: Correctness: M halts ⇒ both languages are Σ*; M does not halt ⇒ L(M1) = ∅ ≠ Σ* = L(M2).
text.zh: 正确性：M 停机 ⇒ 两个语言都是 Σ*；M 不停机 ⇒ L(M1) = ∅ ≠ Σ* = L(M2)。

text.en: H always halts and decides HALT; contradiction; concludes EQ is undecidable.
text.zh: H 总是停机并判定 HALT；产生矛盾；得出 EQ 不可判定。

mistakes.en: Making M1 accept only when M accepts w (not halts): that reduces from the acceptance problem, which is fine, but the answer must then handle rejecting runs of M.
mistakes.zh: 让 M1 仅在 M 接受 w 时接受（而不是停机时接受）：这相当于从接受问题归约，可以，但必须处理 M 拒绝的运行。

mistakes.en: Comparing only on one input, such as 01: equality of languages needs every string to agree.
mistakes.zh: 只在一个输入（如 01）上比较：语言相等要求每个字符串都一致。

mistakes.en: Using the input x in the simulation of M, so that M1's behaviour depends on x and the two cases are not clean.
mistakes.zh: 在模拟 M 时使用输入 x，使 M1 的行为依赖于 x，两种情形就不再干净。

questions.verify_output:
rejects after 7 steps: M halts = True ; L(M1) and L(M2) agree on all sample inputs = True
accepts after 3 steps: M halts = True ; L(M1) and L(M2) agree on all sample inputs = True
loops forever: M halts = False ; L(M1) and L(M2) agree on all sample inputs = False

title.en: The complement of a recognizable, undecidable language
title.zh: 可识别但不可判定的语言的补语言

prompt.en:
Notation: L is recognizable if some Turing machine accepts exactly the strings of L (it may run forever on others). L is decidable if some Turing machine halts on every input and accepts exactly the strings of L. L̄ = Σ* ∖ L is the complement of L.

Suppose L is recognizable but not decidable. What can you say about L̄?
prompt.zh:
记号：若某台图灵机恰好接受 L 的字符串（对其他字符串可以永远运行），L 就是可识别的。若某台图灵机对每个输入都停机并且恰好接受 L 的字符串，L 就是可判定的。L̄ = Σ* ∖ L 是 L 的补语言。

假设 L 可识别但不可判定。关于 L̄ 你能说什么？

text.en: L̄ is decidable.
text.zh: L̄ 可判定。

why.en: If L̄ were decidable, swapping yes and no would decide L. But L is not decidable.
why.zh: 若 L̄ 可判定，交换 yes 和 no 就能判定 L，而 L 不可判定。

text.en: L̄ is recognizable but not decidable.
text.zh: L̄ 可识别但不可判定。

why.en: If L̄ were recognizable, then running recognizers for L and L̄ side by side would decide L (one of them must accept). So L̄ cannot be recognizable.
why.zh: 若 L̄ 可识别，把 L 和 L̄ 的识别器并行运行就能判定 L（二者必有一个接受）。所以 L̄ 不可能可识别。

text.en: Nothing can be said; L̄ may be recognizable or not.
text.zh: 无法判断；L̄ 可能可识别，也可能不可识别。

why.en: The theorem "L decidable iff L and L̄ both recognizable" settles it: here L̄ is certainly not recognizable.
why.zh: 定理“L 可判定当且仅当 L 和 L̄ 都可识别”已经给出结论：这里 L̄ 必定不可识别。

text.en: L̄ is not recognizable.
text.zh: L̄ 不可识别。

why.en: Correct: if both L and L̄ were recognizable, interleaving the two recognizers would give a decider for L. Since L is undecidable, L̄ is not recognizable.
why.zh: 对：若 L 和 L̄ 都可识别，交错运行两个识别器就得到 L 的判定器。L 不可判定，所以 L̄ 不可识别。

solution.en: Think of the pair {L, L̄}: if both halves can be recognized, one of the two recognizers always says yes, so together they decide. Undecidable L therefore breaks at least one half.
solution.zh: 把 {L, L̄} 看成一对：若两半都能识别，两个识别器中总有一个会说 yes，合起来就是判定器。所以 L 不可判定，就至少有一半不可识别。

title.en: A language that is not recognizable

prompt.en:
Notation: a language is recognizable if some Turing machine accepts exactly its members (it may loop on non-members), and decidable if some Turing machine halts on every input and accepts exactly its members. L̄ = Σ* ∖ L is the complement. A_TM = { ⟨M,w⟩ : M accepts w } is recognizable but not decidable (you may use this).

(a) Prove the theorem: if both L and L̄ are recognizable, then L is decidable.
(b) Use (a) to prove that the complement of A_TM is not recognizable.
prompt.zh:
记号：若某台图灵机恰好接受语言的成员（对非成员可以循环），该语言就是可识别的；若某台图灵机对每个输入都停机并恰好接受其成员，该语言就是可判定的。L̄ = Σ* ∖ L 是补语言。A_TM = { ⟨M,w⟩ : M 接受 w } 可识别但不可判定（可以使用这一事实）。

（a）证明定理：如果 L 和 L̄ 都可识别，那么 L 可判定。
（b）利用（a）证明 A_TM 的补语言不可识别。

solution.en:
(a) Let R1 be a recognizer for L and R2 a recognizer for L̄. Build a machine N: on input x, run R1 and R2 on x in alternation, one step of R1, then one step of R2, then another step of R1, and so on. If R1 accepts, N accepts. If R2 accepts, N rejects.

N halts on every x. Exactly one of x ∈ L and x ∈ L̄ is true. If x ∈ L, R1 accepts x after some finite number of steps t1, so N accepts after at most 2·t1 steps. If x ∈ L̄, R2 accepts after some number t2 of steps and N rejects after at most 2·t2 steps. A recognizer can loop on non-members, but the alternation means that the looping one never blocks the other.

N is correct: R1 accepts only members of L, and R2 accepts only members of L̄, so N accepts only members of L and rejects only non-members. So N decides L.

Why alternation matters: if N ran R1 to the end first, it would never get to R2 when x ∉ L, since R1 may run forever.

(b) Suppose the complement of A_TM were recognizable. A_TM is recognizable (it is accepted by the simulation of M on w). By (a) with L = A_TM, A_TM would be decidable. But A_TM is not decidable. This is a contradiction, so the complement of A_TM is not recognizable. ∎

So there are languages for which neither a recognizer nor a decider exists: the "no" side of an undecidable but recognizable problem cannot be confirmed by any machine.
solution.zh:
（a）设 R1 是 L 的识别器，R2 是 L̄ 的识别器。构造机器 N：在输入 x 上，交替运行 R1 和 R2——先走 R1 一步，再走 R2 一步，再走 R1 一步，如此继续。若 R1 接受，N 就接受；若 R2 接受，N 就拒绝。

N 对每个 x 都停机。x ∈ L 与 x ∈ L̄ 恰有一个成立。若 x ∈ L，R1 在有限步 t1 后接受 x，所以 N 至多 2·t1 步后接受。若 x ∈ L̄，R2 在 t2 步后接受，N 至多 2·t2 步后拒绝。识别器对非成员可能循环，但交替运行意味着循环的那一个不会挡住另一个。

N 是正确的：R1 只接受 L 的成员，R2 只接受 L̄ 的成员，所以 N 只接受 L 的成员，也只拒绝非成员。因此 N 判定 L。

为什么必须交替：如果 N 先把 R1 运行到底，那么当 x ∉ L 时它永远轮不到 R2，因为 R1 可能永远运行。

（b）假设 A_TM 的补语言可识别。A_TM 是可识别的（对 M 在 w 上的模拟可以接受它）。由（a），取 L = A_TM，A_TM 就是可判定的。但 A_TM 不可判定。矛盾，所以 A_TM 的补语言不可识别。∎

所以存在既没有识别器也没有判定器的语言：一个可识别但不可判定的问题的“否”一侧，没有任何机器能确认。

text.en: (a) Builds N that alternates single steps of R1 and R2 and accepts if R1 accepts, rejects if R2 accepts.
text.zh: （a）构造 N，交替执行 R1 和 R2 的单步，R1 接受则接受，R2 接受则拒绝。

text.en: (a) Argues N halts on every input (exactly one of x ∈ L, x ∈ L̄ holds, and that recognizer accepts in finitely many steps) and N is correct.
text.zh: （a）论证 N 对每个输入停机（x ∈ L 与 x ∈ L̄ 恰有一个成立，相应的识别器在有限步内接受），并且 N 正确。

text.en: (a) Explains why running R1 to completion first would fail.
text.zh: （a）解释为什么先把 R1 运行到底会失败。

text.en: (b) Assumes the complement of A_TM is recognizable and applies (a) with L = A_TM, using that A_TM is recognizable.
text.zh: （b）假设 A_TM 的补语言可识别，并用 L = A_TM 应用（a），同时利用 A_TM 可识别。

text.en: (b) Contradicts that A_TM is not decidable and concludes.
text.zh: （b）与 A_TM 不可判定矛盾，并得出结论。

mistakes.en: Running R1 first to completion and then R2: this loops forever on strings outside L.
mistakes.zh: 先把 R1 运行到结束再运行 R2：对 L 之外的字符串会永远循环。

mistakes.en: Arguing that the complement is not decidable and stopping there; the claim is stronger: it is not even recognizable.
mistakes.zh: 只论证补语言不可判定就停下；要证的更强：它连可识别都不是。

mistakes.en: Forgetting to use that A_TM itself is recognizable; without it, (a) does not apply.
mistakes.zh: 忘了使用 A_TM 本身可识别这一事实；没有它，（a）就用不上。

title.en: Fill in a truth table for a formula with → and ↔
title.zh: 为含 → 和 ↔ 的公式填真值表

prompt.en:
Notation: p → q is false only when p is true and q is false. p ↔ q is true exactly when p and q have the same truth value. ¬ is negation. Each row names an assignment to (p, q, r): TFT means p = T, q = F, r = T.

Fill in the values of A = p → q, B = q ↔ ¬r and F = A ↔ B for the eight assignments below (write T or F).
prompt.zh:
记号：p → q 仅当 p 为真且 q 为假时才为假。p ↔ q 恰在 p 与 q 的真值相同时为真。¬ 是否定。每一行是对 (p, q, r) 的一个赋值：TFT 表示 p = T、q = F、r = T。

对下面的八个赋值，填出 A = p → q、B = q ↔ ¬r 和 F = A ↔ B 的值（写 T 或 F）。

questions.code:
F = (p → q) ↔ (q ↔ ¬r)
columns:  A = p → q     B = q ↔ ¬r     F = A ↔ B

en: p q r
A = p → q
B = q ↔ ¬r
F = A ↔ B
zh: p q r
A = p → q
B = q ↔ ¬r
F = A ↔ B

solution.en:
Work column by column. A is false only when p = T and q = F (rows TFT and TFF). B = q ↔ ¬r is true when q and r have different values: it is true on TTF, TFT, FTF, FFT and false on TTT, TFF, FTT, FFF. F is true when A and B agree.

Rows (A, B, F): TTT: T, F, F. TTF: T, T, T. TFT: F, T, F. TFF: F, F, T. FTT: T, F, F. FTF: T, T, T. FFT: T, T, T. FFF: T, F, F.

F is true on four rows (TTF, TFF, FTF, FFT), so the formula is satisfiable and not valid (TTT makes it false). Row TFF shows how easily ↔ is misread: F is true there because A and B are both false, not because either one is true.
solution.zh:
逐列计算。A 只在 p = T 且 q = F 的行为假（TFT 与 TFF）。B 在 q 与 ¬r 相同时为真，即 q 与 r 不同时：B 在 TTF、TFT、FTF、FFT 为真，在 TTT、TFF、FTT、FFF 为假。F 在 A 与 B 相同时为真。

各行 (A, B, F)：TTT：T, F, F。TTF：T, T, T。TFT：F, T, F。TFF：F, F, T。FTT：T, F, F。FTF：T, T, T。FFT：T, T, T。FFF：T, F, F。

F 在四行上为真（TTF、TFF、FTF、FFT），所以公式可满足；又 TTT 使它为假，所以它不是有效公式。TFF 这一行提醒我们 ↔ 容易读错：F 在 TFF 为真，是因为 A 和 B 都为假，而不是因为其中一个为真。

questions.verify_code:
from itertools import product
imp = lambda x, y: (not x) or y
iff = lambda x, y: x == y
tf = lambda b: 'T' if b else 'F'
for p, q, r in product([True, False], repeat=3):
    A = imp(p, q)
    B = iff(q, not r)
    F = iff(A, B)
    print('\t'.join([tf(p) + tf(q) + tf(r), tf(A), tf(B), tf(F)]))

title.en: Which formula is equivalent to p → (q → r)?
title.zh: 哪个公式与 p → (q → r) 等价？

prompt.en:
Notation: two formulas are equivalent when they have the same truth value under every truth assignment. → is "if … then" and is false only when the left side is true and the right side is false. → is not associative: p → (q → r) and (p → q) → r are different.

Which formula is equivalent to p → (q → r)?
prompt.zh:
记号：两个公式在每个真值赋值下真值都相同，就是等价的。→ 是“如果……那么”，仅当左边为真而右边为假时才为假。→ 不满足结合律：p → (q → r) 与 (p → q) → r 不同。

哪个公式与 p → (q → r) 等价？

text.en: (p → q) → r
text.zh: (p → q) → r

why.en: Not equivalent. With p = F, q = F, r = F the original is true, but (p → q) → r is T → F, which is false.
why.zh: 不等价。取 p = F，q = F，r = F，原公式为真，而 (p → q) → r 是 T → F，为假。

text.en: p → (q ∧ r)
text.zh: p → (q ∧ r)

why.en: Not equivalent. With p = T, q = F, r = T the original is true (q → r has a false left side), but p → (q ∧ r) is false.
why.zh: 不等价。取 p = T，q = F，r = T，原公式为真（q → r 的左边为假），而 p → (q ∧ r) 为假。

text.en: (p ∧ q) → r
text.zh: (p ∧ q) → r

why.en: Both are false exactly when p and q are true and r is false. (This is "currying": assume p, then assume q.)
why.zh: 二者都恰在 p、q 为真而 r 为假时为假。（这就是“柯里化”：先假设 p，再假设 q。）

text.en: (p ∨ q) → r
text.zh: (p ∨ q) → r

why.en: Not equivalent. With p = F, q = T, r = F the original is true (p is false), but (p ∨ q) → r is false.
why.zh: 不等价。取 p = F，q = T，r = F：原公式因 p 为假而为真，而 (p ∨ q) → r 为假。

solution.en: Find the single falsifying case of the original: p true, q true, r false. The right answer must be false there and nowhere else.
solution.zh: 先找到原公式唯一的使其为假的情形：p 真、q 真、r 假。正确的选项必须恰在这一种情形下为假。

questions.verify_code:
from itertools import product
imp = lambda x, y: (not x) or y
target = lambda p, q, r: imp(p, imp(q, r))
options = {
    'A': lambda p, q, r: imp(p and q, r),
    'B': lambda p, q, r: imp(imp(p, q), r),
    'C': lambda p, q, r: imp(p, q and r),
    'D': lambda p, q, r: imp(p or q, r),
}
for k, f in options.items():
    print(k, all(f(*a) == target(*a) for a in product([False, True], repeat=3)))
questions.verify_output:
A True
B False
C False
D False

title.en: Rewrite a formula to NNF and then CNF
title.zh: 把公式改写成 NNF 再改写成 CNF

prompt.en:
Notation: a literal is an atom p or its negation ¬p. Negation normal form (NNF) uses only ∧, ∨ and negation applied directly to atoms. Conjunctive normal form (CNF) is a conjunction of clauses, each clause being a disjunction of literals. Useful laws: A → B ≡ ¬A ∨ B; A ↔ B ≡ (A → B) ∧ (B → A); ¬(A ∨ B) ≡ ¬A ∧ ¬B; ¬(A ∧ B) ≡ ¬A ∨ ¬B; ¬¬A ≡ A; A ∨ (B ∧ C) ≡ (A ∨ B) ∧ (A ∨ C).

Let F = ¬(p → q) ∨ (r ↔ ¬p). Rewrite F in NNF, showing each step. Then convert the NNF to CNF by distribution, delete clauses that are tautologies (contain some atom and its negation) or that are implied by a shorter clause, and check your final CNF against a truth table.
prompt.zh:
记号：文字是原子 p 或它的否定 ¬p。否定范式（NNF）只用 ∧、∨，且否定只直接作用于原子。合取范式（CNF）是若干子句的合取，每个子句是若干文字的析取。常用定律：A → B ≡ ¬A ∨ B；A ↔ B ≡ (A → B) ∧ (B → A)；¬(A ∨ B) ≡ ¬A ∧ ¬B；¬(A ∧ B) ≡ ¬A ∨ ¬B；¬¬A ≡ A；A ∨ (B ∧ C) ≡ (A ∨ B) ∧ (A ∨ C)。

令 F = ¬(p → q) ∨ (r ↔ ¬p)。把 F 改写成 NNF，写出每一步。然后用分配律把 NNF 化成 CNF，删去重言式子句（同时含某个原子及其否定）以及被更短子句蕴含的子句，并用真值表检验你的最终 CNF。

solution.en:
Step 1, remove → and ↔:
¬(p → q) becomes ¬(¬p ∨ q).
r ↔ ¬p becomes (r → ¬p) ∧ (¬p → r), that is (¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (¬¬p ∨ r).
So F ≡ ¬(¬p ∨ q) ∨ ((¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (¬¬p ∨ r)).

Step 2, push negation to the atoms:
¬(¬p ∨ q) ≡ ¬¬p ∧ ¬q ≡ p ∧ ¬q, and ¬¬p ≡ p.
NNF: F ≡ (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ ((¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (p ∨ r)).

Step 3, distribute ∨ over ∧. Write X = (p ∧ ¬q), Y1 = (¬r ∨ ¬p), Y2 = (p ∨ r). Then X ∨ (Y1 ∧ Y2) ≡ (X ∨ Y1) ∧ (X ∨ Y2).
X ∨ Y1 = (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p ≡ (p ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (¬q ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p).
X ∨ Y2 = (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ p ∨ r ≡ (p ∨ p ∨ r) ∧ (¬q ∨ p ∨ r).
Raw CNF has four clauses: (p ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p), (¬q ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p), (p ∨ r), (¬q ∨ p ∨ r).

Step 4, clean up. The first clause contains p and ¬p, so it is always true: delete it. The clause (¬q ∨ p ∨ r) is implied by (p ∨ r), which has a subset of its literals: delete it.
CNF: (p ∨ r) ∧ (¬p ∨ ¬q ∨ ¬r).

Truth-table check. F is false exactly when p, q, r are all true, or when p and r are both false (q either). The clause (p ∨ r) is false exactly when p = r = F (two rows), and (¬p ∨ ¬q ∨ ¬r) is false exactly on TTT. These are the same three rows, so the CNF is equivalent to F.
solution.zh:
第 1 步，去掉 → 和 ↔：
¬(p → q) 变成 ¬(¬p ∨ q)。
r ↔ ¬p 变成 (r → ¬p) ∧ (¬p → r)，即 (¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (¬¬p ∨ r)。
于是 F ≡ ¬(¬p ∨ q) ∨ ((¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (¬¬p ∨ r))。

第 2 步，把否定推到原子上：
¬(¬p ∨ q) ≡ ¬¬p ∧ ¬q ≡ p ∧ ¬q，并且 ¬¬p ≡ p。
NNF：F ≡ (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ ((¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (p ∨ r))。

第 3 步，对 ∧ 分配 ∨。记 X = (p ∧ ¬q)，Y1 = (¬r ∨ ¬p)，Y2 = (p ∨ r)。则 X ∨ (Y1 ∧ Y2) ≡ (X ∨ Y1) ∧ (X ∨ Y2)。
X ∨ Y1 = (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p ≡ (p ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (¬q ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p)。
X ∨ Y2 = (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ p ∨ r ≡ (p ∨ p ∨ r) ∧ (¬q ∨ p ∨ r)。
原始 CNF 有四个子句：(p ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p)、(¬q ∨ ¬r ∨ ¬p)、(p ∨ r)、(¬q ∨ p ∨ r)。

第 4 步，整理。第一个子句同时含 p 和 ¬p，恒为真：删去。子句 (¬q ∨ p ∨ r) 被 (p ∨ r) 蕴含（后者的文字是前者文字的子集）：删去。
CNF：(p ∨ r) ∧ (¬p ∨ ¬q ∨ ¬r)。

真值表检验。F 恰在 p、q、r 全为真，或 p、r 都为假（q 任意）时为假。子句 (p ∨ r) 恰在 p = r = F 时为假（两行），子句 (¬p ∨ ¬q ∨ ¬r) 恰在 TTT 为假。正好是这三行，所以这个 CNF 与 F 等价。

text.en: Removes → and ↔ correctly, including r ↔ ¬p as two implications.
text.zh: 正确去掉 → 和 ↔，包括把 r ↔ ¬p 拆成两个蕴含。

text.en: Applies De Morgan and double negation to reach an NNF with negation only on atoms.
text.zh: 用德摩根律和双重否定得到否定只在原子上的 NNF。

text.en: States a correct NNF, for example (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ ((¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (p ∨ r)).
text.zh: 写出正确的 NNF，例如 (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ ((¬r ∨ ¬p) ∧ (p ∨ r))。

text.en: Distributes ∨ over ∧ correctly to get a conjunction of clauses (all four clauses).
text.zh: 正确地对 ∧ 分配 ∨，得到子句的合取（共四个子句）。

text.en: Removes the tautologous clause and the subsumed clause, ending with (p ∨ r) ∧ (¬p ∨ ¬q ∨ ¬r) (or an equivalent CNF).
text.zh: 去掉重言式子句和被蕴含的子句，得到 (p ∨ r) ∧ (¬p ∨ ¬q ∨ ¬r)（或等价的 CNF）。

text.en: Checks the result with a truth table or by the falsifying rows.
text.zh: 用真值表或使公式为假的赋值检验结果。

mistakes.en: Pushing ¬ through ∨ without changing it to ∧, for example ¬(¬p ∨ q) ≡ p ∨ ¬q.
mistakes.zh: 把 ¬ 推过 ∨ 时没有把它改成 ∧，例如写成 ¬(¬p ∨ q) ≡ p ∨ ¬q。

mistakes.en: Distributing the wrong way: X ∨ (Y ∧ Z) is (X ∨ Y) ∧ (X ∨ Z), not (X ∧ Y) ∨ (X ∧ Z).
mistakes.zh: 分配方向写反：X ∨ (Y ∧ Z) 应是 (X ∨ Y) ∧ (X ∨ Z)，而不是 (X ∧ Y) ∨ (X ∧ Z)。

mistakes.en: Writing r ↔ ¬p as (r ∧ ¬p) alone, forgetting the other implication.
mistakes.zh: 把 r ↔ ¬p 只写成 (r ∧ ¬p)，漏掉另一个蕴含。

questions.verify_output:
NNF is built from literals, and/or only: True ; equivalent to F: True
raw CNF (4 clauses) equivalent: True ; reduced CNF (2 clauses) equivalent: True
rows where F is false: ['FFF', 'FTF', 'TTT']
tautologous raw clauses: [0]

title.en: Which entailment is valid?

prompt.en:
Notation: Γ ⊨ F means every truth assignment that makes all formulas of Γ true also makes F true. p, q, r are atoms; ∨ is "or", ∧ is "and", ¬ is "not", → is "if … then", ↔ is "if and only if".

Exactly one of these claims is valid. Which one?
prompt.zh:
记号：Γ ⊨ F 表示凡使 Γ 中所有公式为真的真值赋值，也使 F 为真。p、q、r 是原子命题；∨ 是“或”，∧ 是“且”，¬ 是“非”，→ 是“如果……那么”，↔ 是“当且仅当”。

下面的断言恰有一个成立，是哪一个？

text.en: { p ∨ q, ¬p ∨ r } ⊨ q ∨ r
text.zh: { p ∨ q, ¬p ∨ r } ⊨ q ∨ r

why.en: Case on p. If p is true, ¬p is false so ¬p ∨ r forces r. If p is false, p ∨ q forces q. Either way q ∨ r holds. This is the resolution rule.
why.zh: 对 p 分情况。若 p 为真，¬p 为假，所以 ¬p ∨ r 迫使 r 为真。若 p 为假，p ∨ q 迫使 q 为真。两种情况下 q ∨ r 都成立。这就是归结规则。

text.en: { p → q } ⊨ q → p
text.zh: { p → q } ⊨ q → p

why.en: Countermodel: p = F, q = T. Then p → q is true and q → p is false. The converse of an implication is not implied by it.
why.zh: 反模型：p = F，q = T。此时 p → q 为真，q → p 为假。从 p → q 推不出它的逆命题 q → p。

why.en: Countermodel: p = T, q = T, r = F. The premise is true, but p → r is false. "Q or R" does not give both.
why.zh: 反模型：p = T，q = T，r = F。前提为真，但 p → r 为假。“q 或 r”推不出 q 和 r 两者都成立。

text.en: { p ↔ q, q ∨ r } ⊨ p
text.zh: { p ↔ q, q ∨ r } ⊨ p

why.en: Countermodel: p = F, q = F, r = T. Both premises are true, since p ↔ q has equal values and q ∨ r has r, but p is false.
why.zh: 反模型：p = F，q = F，r = T。两个前提都为真（p ↔ q 两边值相同，q ∨ r 靠 r 为真），但 p 为假。

solution.en: To refute an entailment, one countermodel is enough: premises true, conclusion false. To confirm it, argue over all cases or show that premises together with ¬F cannot all be true.
solution.zh: 要驳倒一个后承，一个反模型就够了：前提为真而结论为假。要确认它成立，则要对所有情形论证，或说明前提加上 ¬F 不可能同时为真。

questions.verify_code:
from itertools import product
imp = lambda x, y: (not x) or y
tests = {
    'A': (lambda p, q, r: [imp(p, q)], lambda p, q, r: imp(q, p)),
    'B': (lambda p, q, r: [p or q, (not p) or r], lambda p, q, r: q or r),
    'C': (lambda p, q, r: [imp(p, q or r)], lambda p, q, r: imp(p, q) and imp(p, r)),
    'D': (lambda p, q, r: [p == q, q or r], lambda p, q, r: p),
}
for k, (prem, concl) in tests.items():
    counter = [(p, q, r) for p, q, r in product([False, True], repeat=3) if all(prem(p, q, r)) and not concl(p, q, r)]
    print(k, 'entails' if not counter else 'counter ' + str(counter[0]))
questions.verify_output:
A counter (False, True, False)
B entails
C counter (True, False, True)
D counter (False, False, True)

title.en: Test an entailment with a truth table

prompt.en:
Notation: Γ ⊨ F ("Γ entails F") means that every assignment that makes all premises true also makes F true. An assignment that makes all premises true and F false is a countermodel. Each row names an assignment to (p, q, r): TFT means p = T, q = F, r = T.

Fill in the truth values of the two premises Γ1 and Γ2 and of the conclusion F on the eight rows (T or F). In the last column write yes if the row is a countermodel and no otherwise.
prompt.zh:
记号：Γ ⊨ F（“F 是 Γ 的后承”）表示：凡使所有前提为真的赋值也使 F 为真。使所有前提为真而 F 为假的赋值叫反模型。每一行是对 (p, q, r) 的一个赋值：TFT 表示 p = T、q = F、r = T。

在八行上填出两个前提 Γ1、Γ2 和结论 F 的真值（T 或 F）。最后一列：若该行是反模型就写 yes，否则写 no。

questions.code:
Premises:   Γ1 = p → (q ∨ r)     Γ2 = ¬(q ∧ r)
Conclusion: F = p → q

en: p q r
Γ1
Γ2
F
Countermodel?
zh: p q r
Γ1
Γ2
F
是反模型？

solution.en:
Γ1 = p → (q ∨ r) is false only when p is true and both q and r are false (TFF). Γ2 = ¬(q ∧ r) is false only when q and r are both true (TTT and FTT). F = p → q is false only when p is true and q is false (TFT and TFF).

A countermodel needs Γ1 and Γ2 true and F false. F is false on TFT and TFF. TFF makes Γ1 false, so it is not a countermodel. TFT makes Γ1 true (r is true) and Γ2 true (q is false), and F false. So TFT is the only countermodel.

Therefore Γ does not entail F. One countermodel is enough to show that; listing the rest of the table does not change the answer. If the last column had been all no, the entailment would hold.
solution.zh:
Γ1 = p → (q ∨ r) 仅在 p 为真且 q、r 都为假时为假（TFF）。Γ2 = ¬(q ∧ r) 仅在 q、r 都为真时为假（TTT 与 FTT）。F = p → q 仅在 p 为真且 q 为假时为假（TFT 与 TFF）。

反模型需要 Γ1、Γ2 为真且 F 为假。F 为假的行是 TFT 和 TFF。TFF 使 Γ1 为假，所以不是反模型。TFT 使 Γ1 为真（r 为真）、Γ2 为真（q 为假）、F 为假。所以 TFT 是唯一的反模型。

因此 F 不是 Γ 的后承。有一个反模型就足以说明这一点，表的其余部分不会改变结论。若最后一列全是 no，则后承成立。

questions.verify_code:
from itertools import product
imp = lambda x, y: (not x) or y
tf = lambda b: 'T' if b else 'F'
counter = []
for p, q, r in product([True, False], repeat=3):
    g1 = imp(p, q or r)
    g2 = not (q and r)
    f = imp(p, q)
    bad = g1 and g2 and not f
    if bad:
        counter.append(tf(p) + tf(q) + tf(r))
    print('\t'.join([tf(p) + tf(q) + tf(r), tf(g1), tf(g2), tf(f), 'yes' if bad else 'no']))
assert counter == ['TFT']

title.en: Prove one entailment and refute another
title.zh: 证明一个后承并驳倒另一个

prompt.en:
Notation: Γ ⊨ F means every truth assignment that makes all formulas of Γ true also makes F true. An assignment that makes all of Γ true and F false is a countermodel. p, q, r, s are atoms; ∨ is "or", ∧ is "and", ¬ is "not", → is "if … then", ↔ is "if and only if".

(a) Prove that { p → (q ∨ r), q → s, r → s } ⊨ p → s.
(b) Show that { p → (q ∨ r), ¬(q ∧ r), r → p } ⊭ p ↔ r, by giving a countermodel and checking every formula under it.
(c) In one or two sentences, say why (a) needs an argument about all assignments but (b) needs only one assignment.
prompt.zh:
记号：Γ ⊨ F 表示凡使 Γ 中所有公式为真的真值赋值，也使 F 为真。使 Γ 全真而 F 为假的赋值叫反模型。p、q、r、s 是原子命题；∨ 是“或”，∧ 是“且”，¬ 是“非”，→ 是“如果……那么”，↔ 是“当且仅当”。

（a）证明 { p → (q ∨ r), q → s, r → s } ⊨ p → s。
（b）证明 { p → (q ∨ r), ¬(q ∧ r), r → p } ⊭ p ↔ r：给出一个反模型，并检验在它之下每个公式的真值。
（c）用一两句话说明，为什么（a）需要对所有赋值作论证，而（b）只需要一个赋值。

solution.en:
(a) Take any assignment v that makes all three premises true. We show that v makes p → s true.
If v(p) = F, then p → s is true, and we are done.
If v(p) = T, then the first premise p → (q ∨ r) gives v(q ∨ r) = T. So v(q) = T or v(r) = T.
 Case v(q) = T: the premise q → s gives v(s) = T.
 Case v(r) = T: the premise r → s gives v(s) = T.
In both cases v(s) = T, so p → s is true under v.
Since v was an arbitrary assignment satisfying the premises, every such assignment satisfies p → s. Therefore the entailment holds. ∎
(Another way: a countermodel would need p = T and s = F. Then q → s forces q = F and r → s forces r = F, and the first premise would need q ∨ r = T. This is impossible, so there is no countermodel.)

(b) Take p = T, q = T, r = F. Check each formula:
 p → (q ∨ r) = T → (T ∨ F) = T → T = T.
 ¬(q ∧ r) = ¬(T ∧ F) = ¬F = T.
 r → p = F → T = T.
 All premises are true.
 Conclusion p ↔ r = T ↔ F = F.
So this assignment makes every premise true and the conclusion false. It is a countermodel, and the entailment does not hold. ∎

(c) An entailment claims something about every assignment that satisfies the premises, so proving it means covering all of them (here by cases on p, then on q or r). A single failing assignment refutes that claim, so one countermodel is enough.
solution.zh:
（a）任取使三个前提都为真的赋值 v。我们证明 v 使 p → s 为真。
若 v(p) = F，则 p → s 为真，已完成。
若 v(p) = T，则由第一个前提 p → (q ∨ r) 得 v(q ∨ r) = T，即 v(q) = T 或 v(r) = T。
 情形 v(q) = T：由前提 q → s 得 v(s) = T。
 情形 v(r) = T：由前提 r → s 得 v(s) = T。
两种情形下都有 v(s) = T，所以在 v 下 p → s 为真。
由于 v 是任意满足前提的赋值，所以每个这样的赋值都满足 p → s。因此后承成立。∎
（另一种做法：反模型需要 p = T 且 s = F。那么 q → s 迫使 q = F，r → s 迫使 r = F，而第一个前提又要求 q ∨ r = T。这不可能，所以没有反模型。）

（b）取 p = T，q = T，r = F。逐个检验：
 p → (q ∨ r) = T → (T ∨ F) = T → T = T。
 ¬(q ∧ r) = ¬(T ∧ F) = ¬F = T。
 r → p = F → T = T。
 所有前提都为真。
 结论 p ↔ r = T ↔ F = F。
所以这个赋值使所有前提为真而结论为假。它是反模型，后承不成立。∎

（c）后承断言的是：每一个满足前提的赋值都如何，所以要证明它就必须覆盖所有这样的赋值（这里是对 p 分情况，再对 q 或 r 分情况）。只要有一个赋值使断言失败就足以驳倒它，所以一个反模型就够了。

text.en: (a) Takes an arbitrary assignment satisfying the premises (or assumes ¬(p → s) for contradiction) and says what has to be shown.
text.zh: （a）任取一个满足前提的赋值（或假设 ¬(p → s) 以作反证），并说明需要证明什么。

text.en: (a) Handles the case p false and the case p true, getting q ∨ r from the first premise.
text.zh: （a）处理 p 为假和 p 为真两种情形，由第一个前提得到 q ∨ r。

text.en: (a) Splits on q or r and uses the other two premises to get s; concludes the entailment holds for all such assignments.
text.zh: （a）对 q 或 r 分情况，用另外两个前提得到 s；得出该后承对所有这类赋值成立。

text.en: (b) Gives a correct countermodel such as p = T, q = T, r = F (or another valid one).
text.zh: （b）给出正确的反模型，如 p = T，q = T，r = F（或其他有效反模型）。

text.en: (b) Checks each premise and the conclusion under the assignment, showing premises true and p ↔ r false.
text.zh: （b）在该赋值下检验每个前提和结论，说明前提为真而 p ↔ r 为假。

text.en: (c) Explains that an entailment quantifies over all assignments, so refuting it needs one case, proving it needs all.
text.zh: （c）说明后承涉及所有赋值，所以驳倒只需一个，证明则需要覆盖全部。

mistakes.en: Proving (a) by checking a few assignments only; examples do not prove an entailment.
mistakes.zh: 证明（a）时只检查几个赋值；例子不能证明后承。

mistakes.en: In (b), choosing an assignment that makes a premise false, for example p = T, q = F, r = F (the first premise fails).
mistakes.zh: 在（b）中选了使某个前提为假的赋值，例如 p = T，q = F，r = F（第一个前提不成立）。

mistakes.en: Treating p ↔ r as p → r: the conclusion needs both directions, and the countermodel breaks the direction p → r.
mistakes.zh: 把 p ↔ r 当作 p → r：结论需要两个方向，而反模型破坏了 p → r 这个方向。

questions.verify_code:
from itertools import product
imp = lambda x, y: (not x) or y
tf = lambda b: 'T' if b else 'F'
a_counter = []
for p, q, r, s in product([False, True], repeat=4):
    if imp(p, q or r) and imp(q, s) and imp(r, s) and not imp(p, s):
        a_counter.append((p, q, r, s))
print('part (a): countermodels of {p->(q v r), q->s, r->s} |= p->s:', a_counter)
counters = [tf(p) + tf(q) + tf(r) for p, q, r in product([False, True], repeat=3)
            if imp(p, q or r) and not (q and r) and imp(r, p) and not (p == r)]
print('part (b): countermodels of {p->(q v r), -(q & r), r->p} |= p<->r:', counters)
print('the assignment p=T, q=T, r=F is one of them:', 'TTF' in counters)

part (b): countermodels of {p->(q v r), -(q & r), r->p} |= p<->r: ['TTF']
the assignment p=T, q=T, r=F is one of them: True

title.en: Choose the formula with the right quantifier scope
title.zh: 选出量词作用域正确的公式

prompt.en:
Notation: the domain contains students and courses. Student(x) means x is a student, Course(y) means y is a course, and Takes(x,y) means x takes y. ∀ is "for all", ∃ is "there exists", → is "if … then", ∧ is "and".

Which formula says exactly "Every student takes at least one course"? (The course may differ from student to student.)
prompt.zh:
记号：论域包含学生和课程。Student(x) 表示 x 是学生，Course(y) 表示 y 是课程，Takes(x,y) 表示 x 选修 y。∀ 是“对所有”，∃ 是“存在”，→ 是“如果……那么”，∧ 是“且”。

哪个公式恰好表示“每个学生至少选修一门课”？（课程可以因学生而异。）

text.en: ∀x ∃y (Student(x) ∧ Course(y) ∧ Takes(x,y))
text.zh: ∀x ∃y (Student(x) ∧ Course(y) ∧ Takes(x,y))

why.en: With ∧ directly under ∀x, it claims that every object x in the domain is a student. Courses would also have to be students. It is too strong.
why.zh: ∧ 直接放在 ∀x 之下，等于声称论域里每个对象 x 都是学生，课程也得是学生。这太强了。

text.en: ∃y ∀x ( Student(x) → ( Course(y) ∧ Takes(x,y) ) )
text.zh: ∃y ∀x ( Student(x) → ( Course(y) ∧ Takes(x,y) ) )

why.en: Putting ∃y first forces one single course that all students take. That is stronger than the claim.
why.zh: 把 ∃y 放在最前，就强制存在同一门所有学生都选的课，比原命题强。

text.en: ∀x ( Student(x) → ∀y ( Course(y) → Takes(x,y) ) )
text.zh: ∀x ( Student(x) → ∀y ( Course(y) → Takes(x,y) ) )

why.en: This says every student takes every course. The inner quantifier should be ∃, not ∀.
why.zh: 这表示每个学生选修每门课。内层量词应该是 ∃ 而不是 ∀。

text.en: ∀x ( Student(x) → ∃y ( Course(y) ∧ Takes(x,y) ) )
text.zh: ∀x ( Student(x) → ∃y ( Course(y) ∧ Takes(x,y) ) )

why.en: The implication restricts x to students. The inner ∃y sits after x, so the course can depend on x, and ∧ inside the ∃ says y is a course that x takes. This is right.
why.zh: 蕴含把 x 限制为学生。内层的 ∃y 在 x 之后，所以课程可以依赖于 x；∃ 里面的 ∧ 表示 y 是 x 选修的课程。这是对的。

solution.en: Read from the left: the quantifiers fix who may depend on whom. The student x is chosen first, then a course y may be found for that x. ∀ pairs with → to restrict a group; ∃ pairs with ∧ to name a witness.
solution.zh: 从左往右读：量词的顺序决定谁可以依赖谁。先选定学生 x，再为这个 x 找课程 y。∀ 与 → 搭配来限定一类对象，∃ 与 ∧ 搭配来指出见证。

title.en: Evaluate nested quantifiers on a small structure
title.zh: 在小结构上求嵌套量词的真值

prompt.en:
Notation: a structure gives a domain D and says which pairs satisfy R. ∀x∃y R(x,y) says that every x has some y with R(x,y). ∃y∀x R(x,y) says that one single y has R(x,y) for every x.

For each object x, fill in: the set of y with R(x,y) and whether it is nonempty; the set of y with R(y,x) and whether it contains every object of D. Write a set as {2,3} with no spaces; write the empty set as {}. Write yes or no for the two questions. Then write true or false for φ1 and φ2 in the last two rows (only the second column is used there).
prompt.zh:
记号：结构给出论域 D，并说明哪些对满足 R。∀x∃y R(x,y) 表示：每个 x 都有某个 y 使 R(x,y) 成立。∃y∀x R(x,y) 表示：存在同一个 y，对每个 x 都有 R(x,y)。

对每个对象 x 填写：满足 R(x,y) 的 y 的集合，以及它是否非空；满足 R(y,x) 的 y 的集合，以及它是否包含 D 中所有对象。集合写成 {2,3}，不加空格；空集写 {}。两个问题填 yes 或 no。最后两行用第二列填 φ1 和 φ2 的真假（true 或 false）。

questions.code:
Domain D = {1, 2, 3, 4}
R = {(1,2), (1,3), (2,3), (3,4), (4,3)}      R(x,y) is true exactly for these pairs

φ1 = ∀x ∃y R(x,y)
φ2 = ∃y ∀x R(x,y)

en: x
{y : R(x,y)}
Some y with R(x,y)?
{y : R(y,x)}
Every y has R(y,x)?
zh: x
{y : R(x,y)}
有 y 使 R(x,y)？
{y : R(y,x)}
所有 y 都有 R(y,x)？

solution.en:
Row x = 1: R(1,y) holds for y = 2 and 3, so {2,3}, nonempty. R(y,1) holds for no y (nothing points to 1), so {} and not every y.
Row x = 2: R(2,y) gives {3}; R(y,2) gives {1}.
Row x = 3: R(3,y) gives {4}; R(y,3) gives {1,2,4}. That misses y = 3 itself, because R(3,3) is not in R, so not every y.
Row x = 4: R(4,y) gives {3}; R(y,4) gives {3}.

φ1 = ∀x∃y R(x,y) needs the first "yes" column to be all yes. It is, because every object has at least one outgoing pair, so φ1 is true.
φ2 = ∃y∀x R(x,y) needs some row with yes in the last column, one single y that every x points to. Object 3 is closest (1, 2 and 4 all point to it) but 3 does not point to itself. So φ2 is false.

The same relation makes ∀∃ true and ∃∀ false: the witness y may depend on x in φ1 but must be a single object in φ2.
solution.zh:
行 x = 1：R(1,y) 对 y = 2 和 3 成立，所以是 {2,3}，非空。没有 y 使 R(y,1) 成立（没有任何对象指向 1），所以是 {}，不是所有 y。
行 x = 2：R(2,y) 得 {3}；R(y,2) 得 {1}。
行 x = 3：R(3,y) 得 {4}；R(y,3) 得 {1,2,4}。缺少 y = 3 本身，因为 R(3,3) 不在 R 中，所以不是所有 y。
行 x = 4：R(4,y) 得 {3}；R(y,4) 得 {3}。

φ1 = ∀x∃y R(x,y) 要求第一个 yes/no 列全是 yes。确实如此，每个对象至少有一个出边，所以 φ1 为真。
φ2 = ∃y∀x R(x,y) 要求某一行的最后一列为 yes，即存在同一个 y，所有 x 都指向它。对象 3 最接近（1、2、4 都指向它），但 3 没有指向自己。所以 φ2 为假。

同一个关系使 ∀∃ 为真而 ∃∀ 为假：在 φ1 中，见证 y 可以随 x 变化；在 φ2 中，它必须是同一个对象。

title.en: Translate between English and predicate logic

prompt.en:
Notation: the domain is a set of objects, some of them students and some of them papers (nothing stops an object being neither). Predicates: Student(x) "x is a student"; Paper(x) "x is a paper"; Wrote(x,y) "x wrote y"; Cites(x,y) "x cites y". Equality = is allowed. ∀ is "for all", ∃ is "there exists", ¬ is "not", ∧ is "and", → is "if … then".

(a) Translate: "Every paper was written by at least one student."
(b) Translate: "Some student wrote two different papers."
(c) Translate: "No paper cites itself."
(d) Say in plain English what this means: ∃y ( Paper(y) ∧ ∀x ( Student(x) → Wrote(x,y) ) ).
(e) Say in plain English what this means: ∀x ( Student(x) → ∃y ( Paper(y) ∧ ¬Wrote(x,y) ) ).

For (a) to (c), choose between ∧ and → carefully, and say in one line why.
prompt.zh:
记号：论域是一些对象，其中有些是学生，有些是论文（一个对象也可以两者都不是）。谓词：Student(x)“x 是学生”；Paper(x)“x 是论文”；Wrote(x,y)“x 写了 y”；Cites(x,y)“x 引用了 y”。允许使用等号 =。∀ 是“对所有”，∃ 是“存在”，¬ 是“非”，∧ 是“且”，→ 是“如果……那么”。

（a）翻译：“每篇论文都至少有一名学生写过。”
（b）翻译：“有一名学生写了两篇不同的论文。”
（c）翻译：“没有论文引用它自己。”
（d）用通俗的中文说明这个公式的意思：∃y ( Paper(y) ∧ ∀x ( Student(x) → Wrote(x,y) ) )。
（e）用通俗的中文说明这个公式的意思：∀x ( Student(x) → ∃y ( Paper(y) ∧ ¬Wrote(x,y) ) )。

（a）到（c）要仔细选择 ∧ 还是 →，并用一句话说明理由。

solution.en:
(a) ∀y ( Paper(y) → ∃x ( Student(x) ∧ Wrote(x,y) ) ).
The restriction "every paper" uses ∀ with →, so the claim is only about papers. The witness "a student who wrote it" uses ∃ with ∧: it names an object that is a student and wrote y. The student x is chosen after y, so it may differ from paper to paper.

(b) ∃x ( Student(x) ∧ ∃y ∃z ( Paper(y) ∧ Paper(z) ∧ y ≠ z ∧ Wrote(x,y) ∧ Wrote(x,z) ) ).
Without y ≠ z, one paper could play both roles, and the formula would only say that some student wrote some paper.

(c) ∀y ( Paper(y) → ¬Cites(y,y) ). An equivalent form is ¬∃y ( Paper(y) ∧ Cites(y,y) ).

(d) "Some paper was written by every student." There is one single paper y such that each student wrote it. The ∃y comes first, so y cannot depend on x.

(e) "No student wrote every paper." Every student has some paper that they did not write. The ∃y is after the ∀x, so the missing paper may differ from student to student. It is not the same as "some paper was written by no student", which would have ∃y first.

The pattern: ∀ goes with → to restrict a group; ∃ goes with ∧ to describe a witness. Writing ∀x (Student(x) ∧ …) would say that everything is a student, and writing ∃x (Student(x) → …) is true whenever some object is not a student.
solution.zh:
（a）∀y ( Paper(y) → ∃x ( Student(x) ∧ Wrote(x,y) ) )。
“每篇论文”用 ∀ 配 →，使断言只针对论文。“写了它的学生”这个见证用 ∃ 配 ∧：它指出一个既是学生又写了 y 的对象。学生 x 是在 y 之后选的，所以可以因论文而异。

（b）∃x ( Student(x) ∧ ∃y ∃z ( Paper(y) ∧ Paper(z) ∧ y ≠ z ∧ Wrote(x,y) ∧ Wrote(x,z) ) )。
如果没有 y ≠ z，同一篇论文可以同时充当 y 和 z，公式就只表示“有学生写了某篇论文”。

（c）∀y ( Paper(y) → ¬Cites(y,y) )。等价的写法是 ¬∃y ( Paper(y) ∧ Cites(y,y) )。

（d）“有一篇论文被每个学生都写过。”存在同一篇论文 y，使每个学生都写了它。∃y 在最前面，所以 y 不能依赖于 x。

（e）“没有学生写了所有论文。”每个学生都有某篇论文没写。∃y 在 ∀x 之后，所以没写的那篇可以因学生而异。它与“有一篇论文没有任何学生写”不同，后者要把 ∃y 放在最前面。

规律：∀ 配 → 来限定一类对象；∃ 配 ∧ 来描述见证。写成 ∀x (Student(x) ∧ …) 会说所有对象都是学生；写成 ∃x (Student(x) → …) 则只要有一个对象不是学生就为真。

text.en: (a) ∀ with → on papers and ∃ with ∧ for the student; the student is chosen after the paper.
text.zh: （a）对论文用 ∀ 配 →，对学生用 ∃ 配 ∧；学生在论文之后选取。

text.en: (b) Two witnesses y and z with y ≠ z (equality used), both papers written by the same student.
text.zh: （b）两个见证 y、z 且 y ≠ z（用到等号），两篇论文都由同一名学生写。

text.en: (c) ∀y (Paper(y) → ¬Cites(y,y)) or ¬∃y (Paper(y) ∧ Cites(y,y)).
text.zh: （c）∀y (Paper(y) → ¬Cites(y,y)) 或 ¬∃y (Paper(y) ∧ Cites(y,y))。

text.en: (d) "Some paper was written by every student", with the single paper chosen first.
text.zh: （d）“有一篇论文被每个学生都写过”，那篇论文是先选定的同一篇。

text.en: (e) "No student wrote every paper" (or "each student missed some paper").
text.zh: （e）“没有学生写了所有论文”（或“每个学生都漏写了某篇论文”）。

text.en: Explains the ∀/→ and ∃/∧ pairing and the order of quantifiers in one line each.
text.zh: 分别用一句话说明 ∀/→、∃/∧ 的搭配以及量词的顺序。

mistakes.en: Translating (a) as ∀y ∃x ( Paper(y) ∧ Student(x) ∧ Wrote(x,y) ), which claims everything is a paper.
mistakes.zh: 把（a）译成 ∀y ∃x ( Paper(y) ∧ Student(x) ∧ Wrote(x,y) )，这等于声称所有对象都是论文。

mistakes.en: Dropping y ≠ z in (b), so one paper counts twice.
mistakes.zh: （b）漏掉 y ≠ z，一篇论文被算了两次。

mistakes.en: Reading (d) as "every student wrote some paper", which swaps ∃ and ∀.
mistakes.zh: 把（d）读成“每个学生都写了某篇论文”，这是把 ∃ 与 ∀ 的顺序弄反了。

questions.verify_output:
disagreements {'a': 0, 'b': 0, 'c': 0, 'd': 0, 'e': 0}
each formula is true in some models and false in others True

title.en: Quantifier order: one entailment holds, the converse fails
title.zh: 量词顺序：一个后承成立，其逆不成立

prompt.en:
Notation: a structure consists of a nonempty domain D and a binary relation R on D. The formula ∀x∃y R(x,y) (call it AE) says every x has some y with R(x,y), where y may depend on x. The formula ∃y∀x R(x,y) (call it EA) says a single y has R(x,y) for every x. F ⊨ G means every structure that satisfies F also satisfies G.

(a) Prove that EA ⊨ AE.
(b) Prove that AE ⊭ EA, by giving a structure with a small domain, a relation R, and checking that AE is true and EA is false in it.
prompt.zh:
记号：结构由一个非空论域 D 和 D 上的二元关系 R 组成。公式 ∀x∃y R(x,y)（记为 AE）表示：每个 x 都有某个 y 使 R(x,y) 成立，这里 y 可以依赖于 x。公式 ∃y∀x R(x,y)（记为 EA）表示：存在同一个 y，对每个 x 都有 R(x,y)。F ⊨ G 表示每个满足 F 的结构也满足 G。

（a）证明 EA ⊨ AE。
（b）证明 AE ⊭ EA：给出一个小论域的结构，指定关系 R，并检验 AE 为真、EA 为假。

solution.en:
(a) Let (D, R) be any structure in which EA is true. Then there is an element d in D such that R(e,d) holds for every e in D (this d is the witness for ∃y).
We show that AE holds. Take an arbitrary element e of D. Choose y = d. Then R(e,d) holds, so ∃y R(e,y) is true for this e.
Since e was arbitrary, ∀x∃y R(x,y) is true. So every structure satisfying EA satisfies AE, that is EA ⊨ AE. ∎

(b) Take the domain D = {1, 2} and the relation R = { (1,2), (2,1) }.
AE is true: for x = 1 pick y = 2, since R(1,2); for x = 2 pick y = 1, since R(2,1). Every element has a y.
EA is false: try y = 1. We need R(x,1) for all x, but R(1,1) does not hold. Try y = 2. We need R(x,2) for all x, but R(2,2) does not hold. No element works as a single y.
So this structure satisfies AE and falsifies EA, which shows AE ⊭ EA. ∎

The reason is the order of the quantifiers: in AE the witness y may change with x, and here it does (2 for 1, and 1 for 2); in EA one fixed y must serve every x. A fixed witness gives a varying one for free, but not the other way round.

(A computer check of all relations on domains with 1, 2 and 3 elements confirms that EA ⊨ AE in each of them, and finds structures with AE true and EA false, including this one.)
solution.zh:
（a）设 (D, R) 是任一使 EA 为真的结构。则 D 中存在元素 d，使对 D 中每个 e 都有 R(e,d)（这个 d 是 ∃y 的见证）。
我们证明 AE 成立。任取 D 中的元素 e。取 y = d。则 R(e,d) 成立，所以对这个 e，∃y R(e,y) 为真。
由于 e 是任意的，∀x∃y R(x,y) 为真。所以每个满足 EA 的结构都满足 AE，即 EA ⊨ AE。∎

（b）取论域 D = {1, 2}，关系 R = { (1,2), (2,1) }。
AE 为真：对 x = 1 取 y = 2，因为 R(1,2)；对 x = 2 取 y = 1，因为 R(2,1)。每个元素都有 y。
EA 为假：试 y = 1。需要对所有 x 有 R(x,1)，但 R(1,1) 不成立。试 y = 2。需要对所有 x 有 R(x,2)，但 R(2,2) 不成立。没有任何元素能作为统一的 y。
所以这个结构满足 AE 而使 EA 为假，说明 AE ⊭ EA。∎

原因在于量词的顺序：在 AE 中见证 y 可以随 x 改变，这里确实如此（对 1 取 2，对 2 取 1）；在 EA 中，必须用同一个固定的 y 为每个 x 服务。固定的见证自然给出随 x 变化的见证，反过来却不行。

（用计算机检查含 1、2、3 个元素的论域上的所有关系，结果证实在每种情形下 EA ⊨ AE，并且找到了 AE 为真而 EA 为假的结构，包括这一个。）

text.en: (a) Takes an arbitrary structure satisfying EA and names the witness d.
text.zh: （a）任取满足 EA 的结构，并给出见证 d。

text.en: (a) Takes an arbitrary x (or e), chooses y = d for it, and generalizes to ∀x∃y.
text.zh: （a）任取 x（或 e），为它选 y = d，再推广到 ∀x∃y。

text.en: (b) Gives a valid small structure (domain and R) in which the relation links elements in a cycle or similar.
text.zh: （b）给出一个有效的小结构（论域和 R），例如关系把元素连成环。

text.en: (b) Shows AE is true by exhibiting a y for each x.
text.zh: （b）为每个 x 列出一个 y，说明 AE 为真。

text.en: (b) Shows EA is false by checking each candidate y and finding an x with no R(x,y).
text.zh: （b）逐个检验候选 y，为每个 y 找到使 R(x,y) 不成立的 x，说明 EA 为假。

text.en: Explains the role of quantifier order (witness may depend on x or must be fixed).
text.zh: 说明量词顺序的作用（见证可以依赖 x，还是必须固定）。

mistakes.en: Starting (a) from AE instead of EA, which proves the wrong direction.
mistakes.zh: （a）从 AE 出发而不是从 EA 出发，证明的是错误的方向。

mistakes.en: Giving a countermodel on a one-element domain: with D = {d} the two formulas are equivalent, so no countermodel exists there.
mistakes.zh: 给出只有一个元素的论域上的反模型：D = {d} 时两个公式等价，那里没有反模型。

mistakes.en: Writing a countermodel with a relation that also makes EA true, such as one containing (1,1), (2,1).
mistakes.zh: 给出的关系也使 EA 为真，例如包含 (1,1) 和 (2,1)。

title.en: Diagnostic: finite automata, grammars, computability and logic
